criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use an oblique isometric projection with vertical structures and diagonal ground axes.
Roads and utility routes recede along closely matching diamond directions.
different: Candidate framing is slightly tighter around tall facilities in several crops.
Reference more often preserves a broader surrounding city footprint.

evidence.observation: Diagonal streets and roof planes establish a consistent isometric yaw and pitch.
Ground axes and vertical building faces closely match the reference projection.
The industrial landmark is framed with substantial surrounding city context.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Residential blocks remain subordinate to hospitals, plants, and substations in both.
Utility towers and connection facilities read as larger landmark objects.
different: Candidate hospital towers occupy more of the crop and appear oversized relative to nearby housing.
Reference industrial landmarks spread across wider low-rise complexes with larger chimney and annex silhouettes.

evidence.observation: Hospital scale is elevated but remains integrated with many smaller neighboring buildings.
Two tall hospital blocks dominate the crop more strongly than surrounding residences.
Plant mass is broad, multi-part, and substantially larger than adjacent housing.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use charcoal metal, brown soil, warm amber windows, and cyan utility accents.
Industrial buildings in both have dark roofs and subdued concrete or masonry walls.
different: Reference has richer bronze midtones, sharper highlights, and clearer material separation.
Candidate terrain is darker and more repetitive, with flatter tiled detail and weaker cohesion around structures.

evidence.observation: Bronze soil, blackened plant metal, road surfaces, and amber lights remain distinctly separated.
The matching brown-charcoal palette is present, but surfaces are darker and more uniform.
Industrial metal, concrete, pipes, and illuminated windows carry dense cohesive texture.
